<!-- DO NOT EDIT | GENERATED CONTENT -->

macOS caps how much unified memory the GPU may wire, and vllm-metal sizes
--gpu-memory-utilization as a share of that cap, not of installed RAM. On a Mac
dedicated to serving models the default leaves memory idle.

With no flags, show the current cap and a suggested one. --set raises it now and
installs a LaunchDaemon that applies it again at every boot, since macOS resets
it on restart. The server reads the cap once at startup, so run
'vllm-helper restart' afterwards. macOS only.

## Usage

```console
vllm-helper metal-limit [flags]
```

## Options

### --reset

|      |        |
| ---- | ------ |
| Type | `bool` |

return to the macOS default and remove the boot-time daemon

### --set

|      |          |
| ---- | -------- |
| Type | `string` |

set the cap to this many MiB, or 'auto' for the suggested value

### --yes

|      |        |
| ---- | ------ |
| Type | `bool` |

apply without asking
